title: Cohomology models and retracts of complexes over a field
statement:
Let $F$ be a field, let $D(F)$ be the derived category of cochain complexes of $F$-vector spaces [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and let $H^i$ be its cohomology functors [def-weil-derived-category-cohomology-functor]. A homotopy between chain maps $f,g:P\to Q$ means maps $h^i:P^i\to Q^{i-1}$ with $f-g=dh+hd$; a homotopy equivalence means chain maps inverse up to such homotopies. For any complex $P$, choosing vector-space complements $Z^i=B^i\oplus V^i$ and $P^i=Z^i\oplus T^i$, where $Z^i=\ker d^i$ and $B^i=\operatorname{im}d^{i-1}$, gives a homotopy equivalence between $P$ and its zero-differential cohomology complex $H(P)$ with $H(P)^i=H^i(P)$. Every quasi-isomorphism of $F$-complexes is a homotopy equivalence, and the induced map
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{D(F)}(P,Q)\longrightarrow\prod_{i\in\mathbf Z}\operatorname{Hom}_F(H^i(P),H^i(Q))$$
is bijective. In particular every object of $D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(F)$ [def-weil-point-fd-complexes] is isomorphic to a bounded finite-dimensional zero-differential complex and is perfect [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex].

Let $P$ be such an object and let $e:P\to P$ satisfy $e^2=e$. Then $e$ has a splitting $S\xrightarrow{i}P\xrightarrow{r}S$ in $D(F)$, with $ri=1_S$, $ir=e$, in which $S$ is represented by the zero-differential complex $\operatorname{im}H^i(e)$; the complementary summand is represented by $\ker H^i(e)$. If $v:P\to P$ commutes with $e$, then under this decomposition $ve$ acts as $rvi$ on $S$ and zero on the complementary summand. For two splittings $(S,i,r)$ and $(S',i',r')$ of the same $e$, the map $r'i:S\to S'$ is invertible with inverse $ri'$ and satisfies $(r'i)(rvi)=(r'vi')(r'i)$.

proof.text: For each degree use the complemented modular lattice of subspaces and d²=0 to choose B-disjoint V with B⊔V=Z, and choose a complement T to Z. This proves the existence clause without lifting choices.

For prescribed V,T, form IsCompl V (B⊔T). Extend the cohomology quotient π from cycles to a linear b₀ on the term using injectivity of vector spaces. The restriction c=b₀|V is injective: exactness of P^(n-1)→cycles→homology sends a class-zero v to a boundary, and B∩V=0. It is surjective: write any cycle as b+v and b₀ kills B. Compose c and its inverse with projection onto V along B⊔T and inclusion. Obtain a,b with range a=V, ker b=B⊔T, ab=id in diagram order, iCycles≫b=π, a≫d=0, and d≫b=0. Assemble chain maps. Their first composite is identity and the second induces identity on homology, hence is homotopic to identity by lem-pc-split-category-null-homotopy applied to its difference from identity.

All vector spaces are projective and injective. For any family φ of homology maps, choose sections a of the target π and extensions b of the source π, and set f^n=b_n≫φ_n≫a_n≫iCycles. The differential kills both ends, so f is a chain map. Cancel π and iCycles in homology naturality to verify H^n(f)=φ_n. Two maps with equal homology maps are homotopic by applying lem-pc-split-category-null-homotopy to their difference.

The same null-homotopy lemma makes every complex K-projective: maps into an acyclic complex induce zero on homology. Mathlib CochainComplex.IsKProjective.quasiIso_iff supplies the homotopy equivalence with its hom equal to each given quasi-isomorphism. Its Qh_map_bijective makes every derived arrow between represented objects the localization of a chain map. Hence equal homology maps give equal derived maps by homotopy invariance. Lift arbitrary homology families using the preceding step and the canonical homologyFunctorFactors isomorphisms; use Q.objObjPreimageIso for arbitrary objects. This proves the stated canonical Hom bijection.

Build the zero-differential complex A^n=H^n(P) explicitly. Its homology is canonically A^n via isoHomologyπ and iCyclesIso. Lift these comparison isomorphisms by the Hom bijection; DerivedCategory.isIso_iff makes the lifted arrow an isomorphism. Finite cohomological support gives lower and upper bounds, including empty support, and termwise finite dimension is the given hypothesis. Each term is finite and projective, which proves IsPerfectRingComplex.

For each idempotent cohomology map E, use IsIdempotentElem.isCompl to split range E and ker E. Their inclusions and complement projections satisfy i≫r=id, r≫i=E, j≫s=id, s≫j=id-E, by projectionOnto_comp_subtype and eq_projection. Form the explicit zero-differential complexes of these spaces. Conjugate the inclusions/projections by their derivedZeroIso homology comparisons and lift by the Hom bijection. Injectivity of that bijection proves the four splitting equations in D(F).

From the four splitting equations deduce i≫e=i, e≫r=r, j≫e=0, e≫s=0 and both cross composites zero. Then lift(r,s) and desc(i,j) are inverse by biprod.lift_desc and biproduct extensionality. If v commutes with e, e≫v≫s=0, so biproduct extensionality gives the stated diagonal block formula. For any two splittings, associate their composites and substitute r≫i=r′≫i′=e, i≫e=i, i′≫e=i′. The two comparison composites become identities, and ve=ev proves intertwining.
